_note: Editor data for the serpens-/serpere- family (Latin serpere, 'to crawl, creep'; serpens 'snake'). Limited family: only definitive serpere etymologies included. EXCLUDES: creep/creeper/creeping (from Proto-Germanic *kreupanan, not serpere), reptile/reptilian (from Latin repere, not serpere), serrate (from serrō 'saw'), serf (from servus 'slave'). Placement format with provenance; regenerators MUST preserve by:assistant.

placements.note: A snake; also a malicious or deceitful person (metaphorical extension). From Latin serpēns (creeping thing, snake), present participle of serpere (to crawl).
Resembling or characteristic of a serpent; winding, sinuous. From Latin serpentīnus (of a serpent). Also a green mineral.
